findings.front:
FRONT A: whole-decoder time accounting on today's master. The source is d1fd4405. I checked with git diff that 0769b52f, e3ea69fd and the current master b7734313 all have the same src/, examples/, Cargo.* and sweep.yml as d1fd4405.

FRAME (OBSERVED, runs.jsonl medians). At 2 and 4 threads the decoder is limited by CPU capacity:
- Utilisation, meaning process CPU over (threads x wall), is 0.98-0.996 at 2t and 0.91-0.97 at 4t on every runner.
- At 4t there are 7 threads (4 workers, scan, the read feeder, main) on 4 vCPUs. The mean number of runnable threads waiting is 1.07 (runq 0.368 s over wall 0.343 s, run 41980640481).
- So the 4t wall is roughly the sum of thread CPU, at co-resident rates, divided by (4 x u). On the 8573C, 1 CPU-s removed at 4t is worth 0.26 s of wall.
- Supporting this, #181 moved 4t wall by -3.2% and 4t CPU by -3.5% (run 41979947814, 9V45).

1t STAGE TABLE. The 1t arm is BzReader::new, the sequential reader, pinned to CPU 1. Figures are phases.rs medians in ms of 209.7 MB output (OBSERVED):
| CPU (run) | scan | MTF+RLE2 | build | walk (of which assembly) | RLE1 | CRC | stage sum | wall | residual |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 8573C (41980640481) | 87.8 | 151.0 | 122.0 | 371.9 (19.9) | 19.3 | 9.6 | 761.7 | 802.4 | +40.6 (+5.3%) |
| 9V45 @4.53 GHz (41986885355 attempt 2, base arm) | 49.0 | 81.4 | 68.3 | 131.0 | 7.5 | 11.8 | 349.3 | 365.8 | +16.5 (+4.7%) |
| 9V45 @4.03 GHz (41979947814, head e3ea69f) | 53.6 | 87.7 | 69.7 | 142.9 | 8.1 | 12.7 | 375.9 | 400.5 | +24.6 (+6.6%) |
| 7763 (41988588303, base arm) | 79.4 | 128.2 | 138.9 | 284.5 | 19.0 | 16.7 | 666.8 | 702.2 | +35.4 (+5.3%) |
| 8370C (41986908473, refactor arm 5761a32, about master) | 87.4 | 128.2 | 117.4 | 443.9 | 18.9 | 10.0 | 804.6 | 864.1 | +59.5 (+7.4%) |

Run 41986912287 (7763) shows a +22% residual. It is a noisy run and is excluded.
- The walk's share of 1t time is 37.5-38% on the 9V45, 43% on the 7763 and 49-55% on the Intel runners.
- The residual is the Read copy plus the bench's hash, about 2.5-3% (INFERRED from main's 0.03-0.04 CPU-s at 4t), plus 2-4% that nothing accounts for (a finding).

2t/4t THREAD ACCOUNTING (OBSERVED). CPU-s, medians of 10 rounds. A2 and A4 are the CPU at 2 or 4 threads over the CPU at 1 thread. "unattr" is CPU no sampled thread holds.
| CPU | 2t wall | 4t wall | u2 | u4 | 4t workers/scan/main/unattr | A2 | A4 | 2t->4t |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 8573C | 0.426 | 0.343 | 0.980 | 0.961 | 1.065/0.135/0.030/0.078 | 1.04 | 1.63 | 1.24x |
| 8370C | 0.456 | 0.392 | 0.996 | 0.973 | 1.250/0.140/0.040/0.087 | 1.04 | 1.76 | 1.16x |
| 7763 | 0.389 | 0.324 | 0.990 | 0.953 | 0.990/0.120/0.020/0.094 | 1.09 | 1.75 | 1.20x |
| 9V45 @4.53 | 0.201 | 0.179 | 0.977 | 0.910 | 0.495/0.060/0.010/0.088 | 1.07 | 1.79 | 1.13x |
| 9V45 @4.03 | 0.225 | 0.199 | 0.980 | 0.924 | 0.565/0.070/0.010/0.090 | 1.09 | 1.84 | 1.13x |

The unattributed 6% at 2t and 4t is the sampler's resolution. It reads clock ticks (10 ms) from /proc task stat every 10 ms (examples/ab.rs:76-87, 241-275), so it loses about 10 ms a thread across 7 threads. I spread it across threads by count (INFERRED).

4t WALL-EQUIVALENT (vCPU-s / 4).

8573C, 343 ms. The thread split is OBSERVED; the stage split is INFERRED in two ways (uniform 1.65x inflation, or the 8370C's per-stage factors):
- workers about 1.11 vCPU-s (81%): MTF 58-62 ms, build 50-69, walk 136-153, RLE1 8-10, CRC 4;
- scanner 36.5 ms (10.6%);
- reader/main 10 ms (3.0%);
- feeder and sampler about 4 ms;
- idle 13.5 ms (3.9%).

Applying the 8370C factors to the 8573C's 1t stage times predicts 1.107 s of worker CPU against 1.11 observed. That is consistent but does not discriminate: a uniform factor fits too.

8370C, 392 ms. Co-run factors from the dispatched run 42008210159; decoder wall from 41986908473, a different machine instance:
- MTF 57 ms (14.5%)
- build 75 ms (19.2%)
- walk 178 ms (45.3%, of which assembly 11.5)
- RLE1 11 ms (2.7%)
- CRC 4 ms (1.1%)
- scanner 38 ms (9.7%)
- reader 13 ms (3.3%)
- other 3 ms
- idle 10.6 ms (2.7%)

CO-RUN INFLATION (OBSERVED, run 42008210159, Xeon 8370C @ 3.58 GHz, master b7734313): four phases copies, one per vCPU, against one alone. Each stage is its fastest of 5 passes.

| stage | four copies / alone | range across CPUs |
|---|--:|--:|
| scan | 1.56x | 1.49-1.64 |
| MTF | 1.54x | 1.50-1.58 |
| build | 2.25x | 2.07-2.33 |
| walk, timed split | 1.46x | 1.44-1.49 |
| walk, timed as one | 1.61x | |
| RLE1 | 2.08x | |
| CRC | 1.59x | |
| assembly | 1.77x | |
| total | 1.62x | |

- The walks with per-lane store streams inflate more: the pre-#37 flagged walk 1.95x, the bitmap walk 2.24x. The plain walk inflates 1.56x.
- Under co-run the build's share rises from 14.9% to 20.7% of the stage time, and the walk's falls from 54.0% to 48.8%.

AMDAHL.
- The serial part is about 1.5% of the 4t wall:
  - The stream start is OBSERVED as s.input, a fixed 3.3-4.4 ms at 1, 2 and 4 threads (occupancy 41976148952, 7763).
  - The tail of the last blocks is about 1-1.5 ms (INFERRED).
- Ordered output does not bind. Idle during slot waits was 3 worker-ms at window 16, so a wider window recovers at most 0.3% (41976148952).
- No worker is critical. Workers pull from one queue, and per-thread CPU spreads 0.18-0.31 s in a round while the wall stays at 0.336-0.360 s (41980640481). The scanner binds only from about 7.9-8.8 worker-equivalents (the bench's models).
- s = 0.015 gives an Amdahl ceiling of 3.8x on 4 vCPUs. The observed speedup is 2.0-2.34x.
- 4t/1t efficiency is 58% (8573C), 55% (8370C), 54% (7763) and 50-51% (9V45). On a log scale, of what it loses:
  - SMT and co-residency (A4/A2) is 76-89%;
  - idle is 5-14%;
  - threading and cross-core overhead (A2) is 6-14%.

RESIDUAL AT 4T. The decoder's 4t CPU on the 8370C is 1.521 s. Four co-resident sequential decodes, scaled by the 1t residual factor and the instance difference, need 1.405 s. That leaves +8% the stage costs do not explain. Phases' fastest-of-5 under co-run plausibly accounts for 3-6% of it, so 0-5% is unattributed, across instances.

RANKING by recoverable 4t wall on CI runners:
1. The build's co-run excess: 0-6% (8370C only).
2. Idle beyond the start and tail floor: 0.8-4% (8573C, 7763), up to 7% (9V45).
3. The unattributed parallel-structure excess: 0-4%.
4. MTF: 0-3%.
5. Scanner Huffman: 0-3%, its CPU share only.
6. The post-walk passes: 0-2%.
7. Walk tuning within today's representation: 0-1.5%. A representation change is unknown on CI.
8. The Read copy: 0-1.5%.
9. A wider window or split condition variables: under 0.5% each.

Caveats on the measurements:
- No PMU on any runner, so mechanisms are inferred throughout.
- pmu.yml has never run on master; its one run is 40857395037, PR ci/pmu-probe.
- The bench's 1t arm is the sequential path, so it is not the parallel decoder on one thread. The parallel path on one pinned CPU costs about 4% more on the 7763 (occupancy: 0.729 s against the bench's 0.702 s, different instances).
- The occupancy json labels its slots "2 x threads" while the results show window 4/8/16. The label is stale.
- Instances of one CPU model differ by up to 8% in absolute 4t wall (8370C: #180 base 0.441 against 0.407 between attempts). Cross-instance comparisons carry that uncertainty.

i9-10900K (secondary case):
- No measurement of today's master is recorded.
- The last i9 figures are from 2026-10-28/29 (docs/journal/2026-10-28-workstation-scaling.md:58-62; 2026-10-29-expert-review.md:249-275): 1005-1013 MB/s at 4 workers on v0.1.5-era code.
- On the i9, 4 threads are 4 physical cores with no SMT, and its limit past 4-6 workers was the memory system. CI's SMT decomposition must not be transferred to it.

binding.claim: At 2 and 4 threads the decoder is limited by CPU capacity, not by a serial path. The 4t wall is about the CPU of all threads at co-resident rates divided by (4 x u), and on these runners 4 vCPUs are only about 2.3-2.5 one-thread equivalents. This is the exchange rate every other term uses. On the 8573C, 1 ms of one-thread stage time removed is worth about 0.43 ms of 4t wall with uniform inflation.

Its 4t share rises from about 15% to 19-23%. The excess above the compute baseline, about 0.70 x 2.01 c/B out of 21.8 c/B a copy, is the recoverable bound. The pattern fits many concurrent store streams being what the sibling penalises: the build has up to 256 bucket write streams into a 3.6 MB T-vector and as many read streams over ll. The unstaged flagged walk (1.95x) and bitmap walk (2.24x) show the same pattern; the staged room walk does not. #171's staging of the walk's 32 store streams gained 5-14% at 4t.

binding.claim: vCPU idle at 4t is 2.7-9% depending on the CPU. About 13-16 ms of wall-equivalent is roughly constant in absolute terms across runners, so it is a larger share on the faster 9V45. Of it: about 20% is the fixed stream start (the scanner waiting for the feeder's first 4 MiB chunk, src/read.rs:13,112-133), about 8% is the tail, and about 70% falls mid-stream. Mid-stream, workers sit idle while the scanner reads the block they need (i:rd 2-4% of worker time), and in the handoff (i:q 1-2%). With 6-7 threads on 4 vCPUs the scanner is preempted: it reads 57% of the span, at 0.39 ms elapsed a block against 0.2 ms of one-thread CPU. The window does not bind.

At 4t, the decoder's CPU on the 8370C exceeds four co-resident sequential decodes by about 8%, of which 3-6% is plausibly phases' fastest-of-5 optimism under co-run, leaving 0-5% unattributed. The decoder's per-block decode CPU at 4t/1t is 1.61-1.75x against the four-copy worker-stage 1.63x: preemption about once a block, cross-core symbol and output handoffs, or a 16-slot footprint are the candidates.

binding.claim: The walk is the largest term, about 40-49% of 4t wall, but almost none of it is recoverable within today's representation (32-bit entries, a 3.6 MB T-vector a worker). The 59-setting grid has its optimum at the default, alone and with four copies, on the 9V45 and 9V74. Tile 512 and 1024 failed. The deferred flags cost time. libsais's whole inverse BWT is 1.05x mibz2's. On the 8370C its co-run inflation (1.46-1.61x) is at the compute baseline, so there is no SMT excess to recover on Intel. The post-walk passes (assembly, RLE1, CRC) are about 7% of 4t on the 8370C and are co-run-sensitive there (RLE1 2.08x, assembly 1.77x). That fits #183's fusion showing at 4t only on the 8370C.

verdicts.claim: 1. At 4t the vCPUs are saturated; only 3.3-4.4% is truly unsupplied; the worker-time identity closes twice (run-queue = non-worker CPU, asleep = idle vCPU).
verdicts.reason:
OBSERVED: saturation is real and is not an artefact of the collector. Off mode has no trace and no sampler, and its CPU/wall is 3.846 (r42009406264, 9V74), 3.801 and 3.836 (r41976148952 and r41988588220, 7763), and 3.916 (r41986885416, 8370C).

Four corrections:
(a) The 'two closures' are one equation. In every run line span = wall ± 4 µs, so asleep − idle = 4(span − wall) + (non-worker − run-queue). On the 7763: 0.1736 − 0.1658 = 0.0078 = 0.0519 − 0.0441. With 4 workers on 4 vCPUs, run-queue ≈ non-worker CPU also follows from work conservation whenever the support threads run while the workers are runnable. It confirms saturation; it does not test it independently.
(b) The run-queue inside decode_block is 11.7-12.6% of worker time (0.1170/1.0027, 0.1492/1.1967, 0.1777/1.5207, 0.1523/1.2112). The 13-14% is the whole-life worker run-queue.
(c) The collector contaminates the hi bounds.
- On the 8573C, '3.9% gross' (acct.py) counts the sampler's own CPU as idle. The sampler is pinned on the decoder's CPUs at 4t: 6.2 ms a run.
- '2.8% net' subtracts the sampler twice. ab.rs:602 takes the sampler out of cpu, and ab.rs:988 computes others = (machine busy − that cpu)/span, so the sampler is inside others. others×wall is 6.8 ms against the sampler's 6.2 ms. Every 4t others value is within 1 jiffy (0.025-0.056 CPUs).
- Correct 8573C figure: 3.40%.
- On the 8370C the figure is 2.44% (bench r41976148934 head) and 2.1% (occupancy off), not 1.8-2.9%.
- On the 9V74, the clean figure is 3.9% (off). The 4.5% is the traced full mode.
(d) The lo bound 2xm/(1+m) (about 0.27x on the 8370C) sits far below the only calibration CI has. The window change #180 is supply-only. In 10 paired rounds of r41976148934 (8370C), idle fell from 14.93% to 2.44%, wall fell 8.87% and CPU rose 5.70%. So 0.63 (bootstrap 0.57-0.71) of the closed idle became wall; the rest became SMT CPU inflation. The journal's runs (docs/journal/2026-11-05-window.md:121-125) give 0.59 on the 8370C (wall −8.1%, CPU +6.1%) and 0.72 on the 7763 (−10.3%, +4.3%). The pinned 2t run converted 1.09.

verdicts.claim: 2. Support-thread CPU (above all the scanner's) is the largest lever; 4t wall ≈ total CPU / (4×0.96); about 1.0% of wall per 10% scanner-CPU cut.
verdicts.reason:
The mechanism is pinned by the occupancy run-queue ≈ non-worker CPU (OBSERVED). The wall model's stated check proves nothing: 1.308/3.846 reproduces the wall because 3.846 is the same run's own CPU/wall, and any split that sums to the CPU passes.

Independent support is weak. In r41979947814 (9V45), 4t wall moved −3.25±1.13%, total CPU −3.55±1.19% and attributed worker CPU −4.97±1.39%. Wall tracks total CPU more closely than worker CPU, but only at about 1σ.

The 1.0%-per-10% figure assumes that a worker taking the scanner's sibling slot costs the same CPU per block as the average. On the walk, worker-worker co-residency is expensive: 4 co-running copies run at 6.63 c/B against 2.89 alone, 1.74x aggregate on 2 cores (r41989592674, 9V45). So the figure is an upper estimate.

Two smaller errors:
- The scanner's 4t CPU of 0.135 s is floored to 10 ms ticks (utime and stime separately) and loses its exit sample. The true value is about 0.14-0.15 s, an inflation of 1.6-1.7x, not 1.53x.
- The 0.078 s 'unattributed' is mostly worker CPU (bench/CHANGELOG.md:151-156), not support CPU.
verdicts.corrected_recoverable: ≤1.0% of 4t wall per 10% scanner-CPU cut (upper estimate). The lower end is unpinned until the drain-without-hash arm runs.

verdicts.claim: 3. Start-up: a fixed 1.8-3.4 ms in which every worker idles (4 MiB first chunk, 2 MB lookahead); 0.5-1.1% of CI 4t wall.
verdicts.reason:
OBSERVED, and it reconciles. On the 9V74, s.input is 1.88 ms, w.idle.input is 7.5 ms of worker time (that is, 4 × 1.87 ms), and s.input_workers_busy is 5-7e-6. About 3 idle vCPUs × 1.88 ms = 0.56% of capacity; as a share of wall it is 0.76%.

The 8370C 4t timeline (r41986885416) is flagged by the tool itself: 'perturbs: its trace is not interpreted' (throughput ratio 1.0057, 1.0006-1.0108; examples/occupancy.rs:36-37). Its full mode gives the same 1.86 ms, so the figure stands.

The window copy (extend_from_slice at src/parallel.rs:320) comes after InputGot, so it belongs to the ramp, not to s.input.
verdicts.corrected_recoverable: 0.5-1.1% of CI 4t wall (as B said); 0 at release scale.

verdicts.claim: 4. Steady-state supply losses are all that remain at release scale; the 4t dips come from the scanner waiting in the run queue, not from its speed.
verdicts.reason:
The residual reconciles. On the 9V74, off idle of 3.75-3.9%, less start-up 0.56-0.75%, ramp about 0.2-0.3% and tail about 0.65%, leaves 2.0-2.5%. The mechanism, though, is not pinned.
- The 2t comparison confounds run-queue with headroom. On the 9V74 the scanner reads a block every 0.22 ms against consumption every 0.61 ms at 2t (2.8x); at 4t it is 0.286 against 0.54 ms (1.9x).
- '123-211 ms reading vs 0.13-0.14 s CPU' pairs a 9V74 reading time (123 ms) with a Xeon CPU figure. 123 ms below 130 ms is impossible on one machine.
- The only same-CPU pairing is the 8370C: 211 ms reading against 0.14 s scanner CPU, though from different commits (beef4e8f, c90b3625). It puts about a third of the reading time off-CPU, so the run queue explains about a third of the dips at most.
- The split depends on the collector. On the 9V74, w.idle.reading is 4.15% in timeline mode and 2.65% in full mode, and the handoff is 2.43% against 1.21%.
- The lo of 0.2-0.6% sits below #180's 0.59-0.72 conversion.
verdicts.corrected_recoverable: Steady idle is 2.0-2.5% of capacity on the 9V74. At 0.59-0.72 conversion, that is about 1.2-1.8% of 4t wall: the part that matters at release scale. Cause unresolved (scanner speed vs run queue).

verdicts.claim: 5. Window and ordered output exhausted at window 16 (slot-wait idle 0.13-0.62%, 1.9-3.1 ms of worker time).
verdicts.reason: The conclusion holds, but the numbers are off for the production code. On the 9V74 (r42009406264), w.idle_during_slot_wait_s has a median of 6.5 ms (timeline) and 4.4 ms (full), not 1.9-3.1 ms. Two single timeline runs reach 0.0112 and 0.0100 worker-seconds, so the proposed falsifier threshold of 0.01 already falls inside window-16 noise.
verdicts.corrected_recoverable: ≤0.65% of worker time × 0.6-0.7 ≈ ≤0.4% of 4t wall.

verdicts.claim: 6. Tail: a fixed ~2-2.6 ms wall-equivalent at 4t.
verdicts.reason: It reconciles. w.outside is 7.9-10.5 ms of worker time, 0.62-0.87%. That fits about 1.2-1.5 last blocks (2.17-3.35 ms each) plus the reader catching up. It is INFERRED, and harmless.

verdicts.claim: 7. The scanner is not on the 4t critical path; it would bind only if worker CPU fell 2.0-2.5x; supply idle grows about as 1/block time.
verdicts.reason:
'Not binding today' is pinned: the scanner waits for a slot 40-47% of the span. The k threshold is only a lower bound. Holding R_s (reading time) fixed keeps its run-queue share (about a third on the 8370C), which would shrink as the box unloads. With R_s at the scanner's CPU (0.14 s, 8370C), (1.2716/k + 0.2076)/3.85 = 0.14 gives k ≈ 3.8.

The 'idle × block time ≈ constant' argument cannot tell per-block handoff latency from per-decode fixed costs. On a fixed corpus, wall is proportional to block time, so both scale the same way. It also mixes sampler-on bench idle (9V45, 8370C) with occupancy idle (9V74, 7763).
verdicts.corrected_recoverable: 0 today. The bind threshold is k ≈ 2.0-3.8x.

verdicts.claim: 8. The bench's overlap gap (1.297, 8573C) is about 90% support-thread CPU growing with bytes plus ≤5 ms fixed; wall_n (2998 s) is right, wall_n_fixed (2313 s) under-reads 20-25%.
verdicts.corrected_recoverable: Release 4t ≈ 2998 × 0.98 ≈ 2,940 s. wall_n_fixed under-reads by about 21%.

verdicts.claim: 9. At 1 and 2 threads there is next to nothing to recover from supply.
verdicts.reason: Observed: 2t pinned idle is 2.03% (r41980640481), 0.48% (r41976148934 head) and 1.97-2.29% (r41986885355). The 1t runs show CPU/wall of about 1.00. Note that at 2t the sampler runs on the decoder CPUs' SMT siblings (bench/CHANGELOG.md:168-170), a small collector term on the 2t rows and on the m estimates.

falsifier.missed:
1. The idle-to-wall conversion has already been measured on CI. #180 is the only supply-only A/B. At 4t it turned 0.63 (bootstrap 0.57-0.71) of the closed idle into wall on r41976148934 (8370C: idle 14.93% → 2.44%, wall −8.87%, CPU +5.70%). From the journal's deltas, the other two runs give 0.59 (8370C) and 0.72 (7763) (docs/journal/2026-11-05-window.md:121-125). The paired CPU change of a supply-only arm measures, in aggregate, the 'half-idle vs whole-idle core' question B lists as having no instrument. It makes the lo bound (2xm/(1+m), about 0.22-0.39x) uninformative.

2. The bench's sampler is the collector artefact in B's 4t idle figures.
- At 4t it is pinned on the decoder's CPUs: sampler_cpus is 'pinned' in every 4t row.
- B's gross idle counts its CPU as idle; B's 'net of others' subtracts it twice (ab.rs:602, :988).
- others_busy is never resolvable above 1 jiffy at 4t (0.025-0.056 CPUs).
- Its measured cost to wikidata at 4t is +2.4% and +1.2% of wall, with intervals of ±4% (bench/CHANGELOG.md:162, :166). That is the same order as the whole recoverable idle.
- The 9V45's 7-8% idle exists only in sampler-on bench runs; no occupancy run has landed on a 9V45. Part of it could be the sampler preempting the scanner or reader, the supply threads. This is unmeasured.

3. The unattributed CPU (6% of 4t CPU) is a sampler artefact, mostly worker CPU. It distorts B's claim 8 and the bench model's per-byte worker rate.

4. B's identity is one equation, not two (span = wall ± 4 µs), and work conservation implies most of it when there are as many workers as vCPUs.

5. The tool's own perturbation rule.
- It excludes r41986885416's 4t timeline, which B used for 8370C figures.
- The full-mode 4t cost intervals are wide: −6.6/+3.2% on the 9V74, wider than the idle being split.
- Timeline and full modes split the idle differently by 1-1.6 percentage points (9V74: w.idle 5.7% vs 4.1%).
- The per-cause split of idle is therefore good to about ±1.5 points; only the off-mode total is clean.

6. On a fixed corpus, wall is proportional to block time. 'Idle ∝ 1/block time' therefore cannot tell steady handoff losses, which survive at release scale, from fixed start-up and tail, which do not.

7. Cross-machine pairings: a 9V74 reading time against Xeon scanner CPU, and an idle × block-time table mixing two instruments.

8. Smaller points:
- Bench CPU includes the child's process start-up, which wall excludes (ab.rs:589, startup = 0 for in-process arms). This biases idle slightly low.
- Accounting reconciliation at 4t on the 8573C: 1t CPU 0.804 s, 2t-pinned CPU 0.836 s (1.039x), 4t CPU 1.314 s (1.634x over 1t). This is consistent with SMT sharing at m ≈ 0.24-0.27 net of idle. No unexplained idle remains beyond the 3.4% (sampler excluded).

findings.front: C: the staged room walk (32 lanes, PF_L1 prefetch issued as soon as a lane's row is known, TILE 256, 512 segments; src/bwt.rs:432-434, 1041, 1202 at d1fd4405) on CI's 4-vCPU runners (2 physical cores x 2 SMT siblings) at 1 and 4 threads. The i9-10900K is covered only as a secondary case, and nothing is carried over from it to CI. Verdict: the latency-bound regime is refuted at 32 lanes. On all three AMD models (EPYC 7763, 9V45, 9V74) the walk sits at a per-core memory-side ceiling that one thread already reaches: adding the SMT sibling gives 0.90-0.94x the walk throughput of one thread. On the Xeon 8370C the walk is below its ceiling at 1 thread and fill-buffer-bound (MLP regime) at 4. The walk is about half of 4-thread wall time, but with lines per byte held fixed only 0-5% of 4t wall can be recovered, because the 4-copy walk is already within 6-11% of twice its 1-thread time. Below that floor the only levers are fewer L2-miss lines per output byte (compact30-type footprint) or fewer lines per byte (two bytes per line). On CI, compact30's sign is unresolved: from -16% to +8% of 4t wall depending on CPU and regime, before builder cost.

binding.claim: On the AMD runners (EPYC 7763 Zen 3, 9V45 Zen 5, 9V74 Zen 4) the 32-lane walk is bound by a per-core memory-side ceiling that one thread already reaches. The SMT sibling adds no walk throughput, so at 4 threads each walking worker gets about half of its core's line rate. The interpretation (per-core ceiling) is INFERRED; the ratios are measured.
binding.evidence: Per-core walk step rate, 4 copies over 1 copy (2*t1/t4): 0.94 on the 7763 (phases run 42011789918: 4.33 -> 9.20 c/B), 0.90 on the 9V45 (sweep 41989592674: 2.89 -> 6.44 c/B), 0.94 on the 9V74 (sweep 41989596336: 4.27 -> 9.08 c/B). The 7763's other stages gain from SMT: 5.91 -> 8.26 c/B, a yield of 1.43, so issue width is not what the walk lacks. Lanes past the knee add nothing. 9V74 alone: 24/32 lanes give 4.33/4.27 c/B; 48/64 give 4.56/4.84, slower beyond noise. A fit of t(L) = a + lat/min(L,M) (scripts/fit.py) puts the knee M at 22 alone and 16 per thread at 4 copies on the 9V74 (Zen 4's published 24 MAB: AMD 57647, journal mlp-scheduling:261), and at 32 / 22 on the 9V45. The fitted lat is 47-55 cycles, about the published L3 hit. Without prefetch the knee falls to 22 alone and 12 at 4 copies on both, consistent with a run-ahead window halved under SMT (INFERRED). Prefetch off costs +23%/+48% alone (9V74/9V45) and +40%/+66% at 4 copies.
binding.recoverable_4t_wall: Levers that keep about 1 line per output byte (lanes, hints, segments, tile, shape, loop instructions) are bounded by the gap between the 4-copy walk and twice its 1t time. That gap is +6.2% on the 7763 (<= 3% of 4t wall, <= 9 ms of 0.314 s), +11.4% on the 9V45 (<= 6-7%, <= 12 ms of 0.179 s) and +6.3% on the 9V74 (<= 3.5%). Lower bound 0: none of the 59 sweep settings is faster beyond noise, alone or at 4 copies, on either runner (docs/journal/2026-11-05-coresident-walk.md:88-97). Central 0-1%.
binding.share_of_4t_wall: 7763: the walk is 52.7% of the 4-copy stage time (OBSERVED), times 93% of worker time decoding (occupancy 41976148952), so about 49% of 4t wall. 9V45/9V74: about 50-60%, INFERRED as 1t stage share x sweep 4-copy factor / decoder worker CPU (9V45: 0.625 ns/B x 2.23 = 1.39 against 2.34-2.77 ns/B of worker CPU).
binding.term_path: walk step -> one random T-vector line (one per byte; plain chain 40.8 cycles on the 7763 matches 0.14 x 14 + 0.86 x 46, so there is no reuse of lines between steps) -> per-core miss-handling or L2-to-L3 fill capacity shared by both siblings
binding.falsifier: Two copies pinned to siblings (CPUs 0,1) reaching >= 1.2x one copy's per-core walk rate; or any walk-loop setting faster beyond noise in a 4-copy sweep on a Zen 3/4/5 runner.

binding.claim: The latency-bound regime does not bind at 32 lanes on any CI model measured. Each lane's prefetch completes about a full round before its demand load, so the misses are borne by prefetches and latency is not exposed per step. Prefetch distance is not a lever: in a pointer chain each lane's lead is fixed at one step, and only the lane count lengthens it.
binding.evidence: Single-chain latency, from the plain walk (src/bwt.rs:410): 40.8 -> 47.9 cycles/step on the 7763 (+17%) and 43.9 -> 68.3 on the 8370C (+56%), alone vs 4 copies (phases runs 42011789918, 42008210159). The latency-bound prediction, chain latency / 32, gives 1.27 / 1.50 c/B on the 7763 (1t / 4 copies) against 4.33 / 9.20 measured, and 1.37 / 2.13 on the 8370C against 7.27 / 10.64. On the AMD runners it also predicts the wrong 4-copy/1-copy ratio: 1.12-1.18 against 2.12-2.23. One round, 32 x t, is 139 / 294 cycles on the 7763 (1t / 4 copies), 233 / 341 on the 8370C and 92 / 206 on the 9V45, which is 2.9-6x the loaded chain latency. The prefetch is issued when the row is known (src/bwt.rs:1041), so the line is in L1 when the lane's turn comes. The exception is a tile that evicts it: TILE 1024 (32 KiB) on Zen 4's 32 KiB L1D cost +23.5% at 1t (docs/journal/2026-11-05-tile-size.md:93).
binding.recoverable_4t_wall: 0-1%: prefetch placement, lead and hint. L2, NTA and late variants tie or lose (docs/journal/2026-11-05-walk-round.md:82; coresident-walk.md:79-97).
binding.share_of_4t_wall: none separable: exposed latency per step is about 0 on average
binding.term_path: walk -> per-lane dependent chain -> prefetch lead = one round -> hidden
binding.falsifier: Counters showing more than about 20% of demand loads hitting lines still in flight at 4 copies, or a longer-lead variant faster beyond noise. Neither is measurable on CI today (no PMU).

binding.claim: On the Xeon 8370C (Ice Lake SP) the walk is fill-buffer-bound (the MLP regime) at 4 threads but below its ceiling at 1 thread. Here SMT helps the walk, and the build is the stage that loses from it.
binding.evidence: Phases run 42008210159. The walk's SMT yield is 1.37 (7.27 alone -> 10.64 c/B at 4 copies); the build's is 0.89 (2.01 -> 4.52). The effective in-flight count (plain/room) is 6.0 per thread alone and 6.4 per thread = 12.8 per core at 4 copies, about Sunny Cove's 12 fill buffers. The MLP prediction for 4 copies, loaded chain 68.3 cycles / (12/2 FB per thread) = 11.4 c/B, is within 7% of the measured 10.64. At 1t the same model predicts 43.9/12 = 3.66 against 7.27 measured, so one thread uses only about half the fill buffers. The cause of that is unknown.
binding.recoverable_4t_wall: From the walk loop at 4t: 0 to about 3% of wall (at the fill-buffer ceiling within the model's 7%). From the build: outside this front, but its x2.25 at 4 copies (20.7% of 4-copy stage time) is the larger SMT penalty on this model.
binding.share_of_4t_wall: 48.8% of 4-copy stage time, about 45% of 4t wall (0.39 s, run 41986908473)
binding.term_path: walk -> line per step -> 12 L1 fill buffers per core shared by siblings
binding.falsifier: A fill-buffer-light variant (for example an L2-hinted prefetch, which per the Intel manual does not hold a fill buffer, journal mlp-scheduling:270) faster beyond noise at 4 copies on an 8370C.

binding.claim: The walk's share of 4t wall is not its recoverable time. Its 4t floor is (L2-miss lines per output byte) x (per-core ceiling, halved per sibling). Below the gap in the first entry, its 4t time can fall only through more L2 hits (a smaller table) or fewer lines per byte. At 4t each core holds two 3.6 MB T-vectors in a 0.5-2 MB L2, and on Zen 3 the walk's lines still come almost entirely from the on-chip L3.
binding.evidence: T-vector 4n = 3.6 MB per full block. The 233 blocks of at least 64Ki rows hold 99.996% of rows (journal mlp-scheduling:207). Live at 4t: mean 2.85 of 4 T-vector phases, 10.3 MB mean, 14.4 MB max (occupancy 41976148952). Per core at 4t: 7.2 MB against an L2 of 0.5 MB (Zen 3), 1 MB (Zen 4/5, PMU probe 40857395037), 1.25 MB (ICX) or 2 MB (EMR). Uniform-random L2 hit rates, 1t/4t: 0.14/0.07, 0.28/0.14, 0.35/0.17, 0.56/0.28. On the 7763 the plain chain's 40.8 cycles matches 0.14 x 14 + 0.86 x 46 (L3, AMD 56665), and its rise to 47.9 at 4 copies is accounted for by the L2 loss (+2.4 cycles) plus a DRAM share of no more than about 2%. Line-rate ceilings: published capacities with the measured chain latency underpredict the AMD walk 2.3-2.5x. That makes AMD's effective capacity about 10 per core (plain/room: 9.4 alone, 10.4 per core at 4 copies), or else the loaded latency is about 2.4x the chain latency. An L2-to-L3 fill bandwidth model (32 B/cycle per core, 2 lines per L2 miss if Zen's L2 up/down prefetcher fetches a pair, journal mlp-scheduling:296) matches the 9V45 at 2.89/6.89 against 2.89/6.44 measured. It is 1.25-1.5x off on Zen 3/4, and the factor of 2 is unverified.
binding.recoverable_4t_wall: Bounded only by changing lines. For example, half the lines per byte (a two-bytes-per-line walk) would halve the 4t walk: up to -22% to -30% of 4t wall, before its added step and build cost.
binding.share_of_4t_wall: about 45-49% measured (8370C, 7763); about 50-60% inferred (9V45, 9V74); 55-67% bound on the 8573C (its whole-decoder 4t amplification of 1.62 caps the walk's factor at about 2.1-2.3 if the other stages amplify 1.0-1.15x)
binding.term_path: walk -> lines per byte (about 1) x L2 hit rate (footprint per core) x per-core ceiling
binding.falsifier: A table with the same lines per step but a higher L2 hit rate (for example, the walk over an L2-resident 0.75 MB synthetic table in the 4-copy sweep) that is not faster per step at 4 copies.

binding.claim: Compact30 (64-byte records of 30 entries plus a RAW area, about 2.13-2.164 B/entry: 1.92-1.95 MB a block, 3.8-3.9 MB per core at 4t) still costs one line per step. In the regime that fits CI, the per-core ceiling, it changes the 4t walk only through the L2 hit rate. Its added step work (21 vs 16 instructions, 4 vs 3 loads in the prototype; blog 2026-11-02 :1593) is free only to the extent that the ceiling binds. On CI its sign is unresolved.
binding.evidence: 4t, two tables per core (scripts/model.py), optimistic / pessimistic (L2 share 0.6). Fill bandwidth model, L2-miss lines: Zen 3 -6.6% / -3.8%; Zen 4/5 -14.2% / -8.0%; ICX -18.4% / -10.2%; EMR about -33% / -17%. MLP model, miss occupancy, using the measured loaded chain where available: Zen 3 -4.5% / -2.7%; Zen 4/5 -9.8% / -5.6%; ICX -14.1% / -7.9%; EMR about -26% / -14% (assuming an SPR-like 33 ns L3). Latency-bound model: the same latency change, but the +31% step instructions are exposed. The i9 measured exactly that cost at 1 core, 1.148x (blog 2026-11-02:1624). The i9's 4-worker 0.840x (:1625) came from the shared-L3 capacity mechanism, on 4 separate cores with a 20 MiB L3 and 256 KB L2, where latency rose 49% at constant MLP. On CI that mechanism has at most the 7763's +17% chain-latency rise (or the 8370C's +56%) to act on.
binding.recoverable_4t_wall: If the step overhead is fully hidden: Zen 3 -1.3% to -3.2% of 4t wall; Zen 4/5 -2.8% to -7%; ICX -3.5% to -9%; EMR -5% to -16% (regime unmeasured there). If the overhead is exposed as on the i9 at 1 core: up to +5% to +8%. The builder's cost comes on top: today's build is 17.6% (7763) and 20.7% (8370C) of 4-copy stage time, so each +10% of build adds about +2% of wall. Net bound across CI models: -16% to +8%, central -1% to -4% on Zen 4/5 and ICX, about 0 on Zen 3.
binding.share_of_4t_wall: acts on the walk's about 45-60% of 4t wall
binding.term_path: walk -> table footprint per core -> L2 hit rate -> per-core ceiling; plus the step's added instructions and loads
binding.falsifier: A compact30 staged-walk row in the 4-copy sweep on a Zen 4/5 runner that is not faster than room/32/L1 beyond noise. That would refute the L2-capacity gain on CI. It is a walk-only test, so it needs no builder.

binding.claim: Most of the walk's 4t penalty on CI comes from the SMT sibling sharing a core, not from the other core or the shared L3. VM-wide footprint levers, the i9's mechanism, have little to act on here.

findings.unknowns: (1) What the AMD per-core ceiling actually is: miss-buffer capacity at a loaded latency of about 2.4x the single chain (the effective about 10 per core is well under the published 24 MAB), or L2-to-L3 fill bandwidth at about 2 lines per L2 miss from the up/down prefetcher (this fits the 9V45 at 1t and 4 copies, but is 1.25-1.5x off on Zen 3/4). Both predict the same sign for footprint changes and differ on how much an L2 hit saves. CI has no PMU to separate them. (2) Zen 5's L1 miss-buffer count: no primary source found. (3) The 8573C (Emerald Rapids) at 4 copies: no walk or phases measurement exists, and its L3 latency is unknown (Sapphire Rapids is about 33 ns). (4) Why the 8370C uses only about 6 of 12 fill buffers at 1t with 32 lanes. (5) The share of the VM's visible 32 MB L3 that is actually usable alongside other tenants, and the DRAM share at 4t. That share is bounded at about 2% on the 7763 by the plain chain's +7 cycles; the 8370C's +24 cycles is unattributed (L3/mesh vs DRAM). (6) The sibling-vs-cross-core split of the walk's x2.1-2.2 is bounded only indirectly, through whole-decoder 2t amplification. (7) The 4-copy phases figures are fastest of 5 passes, which biases them low against the sweep's median of rounds, so the 7763 and 8370C factors may be understated. (8) The compact30 staged walk and builder have never run on CI; their cost there is unknown. (9) TLB terms are unmeasured. (10) Zen 3's 512 KiB L2 is from AMD's specification, not probed on the 7763 in these runs.

verdicts.claim: AMD (EPYC 7763 / 9V45 / 9V74): the 32-lane walk sits at a per-core memory-side ceiling that one thread already reaches; the SMT sibling adds no walk throughput (2*t1/t4 = 0.94 / 0.90 / 0.94).
verdicts.reason:
The ratios and gaps reproduce (+6.2 / +11.4 / +6.3%). The regime is contradicted by C's own runs, on five counts.
(a) KERNEL TEST, OBSERVED (phases 42011789918, 7763). Plain, bitmap, flagged and room walks all read about one random T line per byte. Their 1t line rates are 0.025 / 0.071 / 0.145 / 0.231 lines a cycle, and their 4-copy factors are x1.18 / x2.16 / x2.13 / x2.12. At 4 copies the bitmap walk draws at most 0.065 lines a cycle per core, 28% of what the memory side gave one room thread alone, and still loses x2.16. A per-core line-rate ceiling cannot impose the same x2.1 on kernels 3.3x apart in line rate. The factor follows each kernel's own per-byte work. The sweeps agree: flagged/32/L1 goes 4.37 -> 11.78 (x2.69) on the 9V45 and 6.82 -> 14.57 (x2.14) on the 9V74. That is at most 0.170 and 0.137 lines a cycle per core, against 0.346 and 0.234 delivered to one room thread.
(b) LANE TEST, OBSERVED (sweeps 41989592674 and 41989596336; C's own fit.py). The 4-copy time minus the alone time, at 8 / 12 / 16 / 24 / 32 lanes, is +2.75 / +2.79 / +3.06 / +2.91 / +3.55 c/B on the 9V45 and +3.91 / +3.75 / +3.97 / +4.65 / +4.80 on the 9V74. The drop from 8 to 16 lanes is the same alone and at 4 copies (2.99 vs 2.68; 3.35 vs 3.29). The fitted lat does not change (47.1 -> 44.6 and 52.0 -> 54.8 cycles), while the intercept a goes 1.43 -> 4.49 and 2.12 -> 5.68. At 8 lanes the two siblings hold at most 16 chains and at most 0.198 lines a cycle per core, yet pay 77-81% of the 32-lane penalty. A miss-capacity, fill-bandwidth or latency ceiling would leave the low-lane rows nearly untouched. At most (3.55-2.75)/6.44 = 12% (9V45) and (4.80-3.91)/9.08 = 10% (9V74) of the 4-copy walk is lane-dependent.
(c) DUTY, INFERRED from OBSERVED shares. No CI figure is a walk measured against a walking sibling. In the 4-copy production pass the sibling walks 9.20/17.46 = 53% of its time on the 7763 (49% on the 8370C). In occupancy 41976148952, the mean number of workers in the T-vector phase is 2.85 of 4. Under C's model the 4-copy factor would then be 1/(1-d/2) = 1.36-1.40, not 2.12-2.23. So 2*t1 is not the floor even within C's own model.
(d) OBSERVED. #181 (d1fd4405) does not change lines per byte, yet it made the 1t walk stage -6.8% (-9.8, -3.8) faster on a 9V45 (pr181-run3) and -2.6% (-4.3, -0.8) faster on a 9V74 (pr181-run1). One thread is therefore not at a memory-side ceiling.
(e) VENDOR. Zen 5 'can track up to 124 outstanding in-flight cache misses' (58455 section 2.12). Zen 3 and Zen 4 track 24 in the MAB (56665 and 57647, section 2.12). Yet the 9V45 has the lowest SMT yield of the three (0.90). The Little's-law in-flight count at 1t is 9.4/24 (7763), 12.2/24 (9V74) and 16.3/124 (9V45): 39%, 51% and 13% of capacity.
(f) VENDOR SMT TABLES (56665 Table 3, 57647 Table 4, 58455 Table 10, section 2.14). Memory request buffers, the load queue and the schedulers are watermarked, not freely shared. The store queue (64 / 64 / 104 entries), the retire queue (256 / 320 / 448, half each per thread) and the op queue are statically partitioned. C never considered this documented per-thread halving.
INFERRED replacement: core-side SMT contention. The walk loop saturates some core structure at 1t and splits it with the sibling. Which structure is unpinned without a PMU.
verdicts.corrected_recoverable: Not 0-5%. On AMD the 4-copy walk is about 2.1-2.2x its 1t time across kernels (7763: three kernels at x2.12-2.16). So a cut of x in the 1t walk that keeps lines per byte fixed carries over about 1:1 to the 4t walk, which is about 0.5x of 4t wall. Check: #181's -6.8% on the 1t walk predicts -3.4% of 4t wall; the bench measured -3.2% (-5.6, -0.7) on the 9V45. Bounds: lo 0. Theoretical hi = the walk's SMT excess, 53-55% of the 4-copy walk, which is about 26-33% of 4t wall. Single past changes realized 3% (#181) and 5-14% (#171, 4t wall).

verdicts.claim: The latency-bound regime does not bind at 32 lanes on any CI model; exposed latency per step is about 0; prefetch distance is not a lever.
verdicts.reason:
The mechanism fails; the 4t prediction stands.
- C's own fit is additive, t = a + lat/min(L, M). Its latency term is 47.1/32 = 1.47 c/B of 2.89 (51%) on the 9V45 alone and 52.0/22 = 2.36 of 4.27 (55%) on the 9V74 alone. That is an exposed latency term, not about 0.
- On the 9V45 alone, 24 lanes is +19.0% (+14.5, +23.6) slower than 32. Its round, 24 x 3.45 = 83 cycles, is already 1.8x the fitted 47-cycle latency. And 48 lanes is -3.3% (-10.0, +3.9). So the inference 'round >> chain latency, therefore latency is hidden' fails on Zen 5 at 1t. A falsifier already exists without counters.
- At 4 copies every AMD curve is flat from 24 to 64 lanes, so 0 at 4t survives.
- Missed: without prefetch, the 4-copy walk is flat at 10.5-10.9 c/B (9V45) and 12.1-12.9 (9V74) from 12 to 64 lanes. Prefetch's value grows under SMT: none-vs-L1 goes +48% -> +66% on the 9V45 and +23% -> +40% on the 9V74. That fits the statically partitioned retire queue (128 / 160 / 224 entries a thread) halving the out-of-order window, with software prefetch decoupling MLP from it (INFERRED).
verdicts.corrected_recoverable: 4t: 0-1% from lanes, hints, segments and prefetch lead. No 4-copy setting is faster beyond noise (coresident-walk.md:88-97). 1t on Zen 5: 0-3% (48 lanes, -3.3%, n.s.), which is not 4t wall.

verdicts.claim: Xeon 8370C (Ice Lake SP): the walk is fill-buffer-bound (MLP regime) at 4 threads and below its ceiling at 1 thread; SMT helps the walk, and the build loses.
verdicts.reason:
The fill-buffer part does not hold. The build's x2.25 (2.01 -> 4.52 c/B) stands as an observation.
(a) KERNEL TEST, OBSERVED (phases 42008210159). Bitmap (x2.24) and flagged (x1.95) lose more than room (x1.46). Yet by Little's law with plain4, their per-core in-flight at 4 copies is 4.0 and 7.3, far under 12 fill buffers. The walks with the most work per byte lose the most.
(b) Room's per-thread in-flight barely changes, 6.0 -> 6.4. Both walk only about 49% of the time (duty), and 6 + 6 reaches 12 only then, so the fill-buffer cap is never needed.
(c) plain4 (68.3 cycles) is measured while the siblings run plain passes. phases.rs runs each unused walk's passes on their own, after the production passes. So plain4 is not the room walk's loaded latency. A heavier co-load would put in-flight at 12.8 or more a core, over the asserted cap; the 'within 7%' is 7% faster than a hard 12-buffer bound allows.
(d) VENDOR. ORM 248966-050 gives no Ice Lake fill-buffer count. Its Golden Cove section says only 'Increase of outstanding misses (16 FB, 32->48 Deeper MLC miss queues)'. So Sunny Cove has fewer than 16 fill buffers and a 32-entry MLC miss queue; the figure 12 is secondary. The L2 spatial prefetcher pairs lines (248966-046, via the journal), so at most about 16 walk misses fit the MLC queue.
(e) In the same run, 'room (used)' is x1.46 and 'room + assembly as one' is x1.61, so the 4-copy factor carries about +/-10% noise and the yield is 1.24-1.37.
(f) No lane sweep exists on any Intel runner.
(g) The 1t 'cause unknown' is Little's law. A round is 32 x 7.27 = 233 cycles against a 44-cycle chain, so the 6 in flight is an output of a core-side rate, not a limit.
verdicts.corrected_recoverable: The regime is unresolved: core-side or constant-MLP latency, not shown to be fill-buffer-bound. Walk levers: lo 0, hi about 14% of 4t wall (the room walk's SMT excess, 3.38 of 10.64 c/B, times about 45% walk share). The build's +2.51 c/B at 4 copies (OBSERVED) is the larger SMT term on this model.

verdicts.claim: The walk's 4t floor is L2-miss lines per byte times the per-core ceiling; below the gap only more L2 hits or fewer lines per byte help; a two-bytes-per-line walk would cut 22-30% of 4t wall.
verdicts.reason: It inherits verdict 1's refuted regime. In C's own fit, the lane-dependent (memory) part of the 4-copy walk is lat/M = 2.03 of 6.44 c/B (32%, 9V45) and 3.43 of 9.08 (38%, 9V74). The remainder is the lane-independent SMT term. Changes that keep the lines fixed have moved 4t: #171 (store pattern, same lines) -5% to -14%, and #181 -3.2%. Halving lines halves steps, but the pair step's work lands on the binding core-side term. #6 and #34 lost on CI EPYC. Vendor nit: the Zen 3 L2 is 'no less than 12 cycles' (56665 section 2.6.3), not 14. That gives 0.14 x 12 + 0.86 x 46 = 41.2 instead of 41.5, which changes nothing.
verdicts.corrected_recoverable: Footprint and line levers act only on the 32-38% memory term, a theoretical hi of about 15-19% of 4t wall. An L2-hit change like compact30's (hit rate 0.14 -> 0.26, average latency about -10%) recovers about 1.5-2% of 4t wall. Pair walk: sign unknown; the -22 to -30% has no support.

verdicts.claim: Compact30 at 4t changes the walk only through the L2 hit rate; its added step work is free to the extent the ceiling binds; net -16% to +8% of 4t wall, central -1% to -4% on Zen 4/5 and ICX.
verdicts.reason: The binding 4t term on AMD is lane-independent work: a4 = 4.49 and 5.68 c/B, 70% and 63% of the 4-copy walk. That is exactly where +31% step instructions and a 4th load a step land. The phases kernel rows show the 4-copy walk time tracking per-byte work. Ir is not proportional (#181: +4% Ir and faster), so the size of the hit is uncertain, but it is not hidden. The EMR -5% to -16% has no 4-copy measurement under it.
verdicts.corrected_recoverable:
Zen 4/5, 4t wall before the builder:
- if a4 scales with step work: walk +15.6% (9V74) / +18.6% (9V45), about +8% to +11% of wall;
- if a4 does not scale at all: walk -3.7% / -3.0%, about -2%.
Range -2% to +11%, central about +3% to +5% (slower). Add about +2% of wall for each +10% of build cost. Zen 3: same sign, with a smaller L2 gain (0.07 -> 0.13). Intel models: no regime basis for any figure.

verdicts.claim: Most of the walk's 4t penalty is from the SMT sibling, not the other core or L3; cross-core and L3 terms are at most about 2-6% of 4t wall.
verdicts.reason: The 2-thread pinning is real: --spread uses one CPU a core (examples/ab.rs:19, 718-720; test spread_list(cores, 2) == "0,2"). The arithmetic checks: 1 + 0.04/0.42 = 1.10 and 1 + 0.11/0.42 = 1.26. Verdict 1 sharpens it: the per-core part is core-side, not memory-side. The 7763's 2t figure comes from a noisy run.
verdicts.corrected_recoverable: As stated: at most about 2-6% of 4t wall from VM-wide footprint changes.

verdicts.claim: Instruction counts do not predict the walk's 4t time; cuts inside the loop buy nothing, being hidden under the ceiling (#168, #173, #181).
verdicts.reason:
Only 'Ir is not the predictor' survives (#181: +4% Ir and faster).
- #168 (-2.6% Ir) and #173 (-2.0%) could move 4t wall by at most about 1.3% even if fully proportional. Their 4t half-widths were +/-1.8-2.1% (pr168, 7763 and 9V74) and +/-1.55% / +/-5.2% (pr173, 7763 and 9V45). 'No gain' is an unresolved result, not a null.
- #181 is a walk-loop change that cut 4t wall by -3.2% (-5.6, -0.7) on the 9V45. That meets C's own falsifier for claim 1 ('any walk-loop setting faster beyond noise... on a Zen runner') through the decoder bench.
- 'Hidden under the ceiling' falls with verdict 1.
- The same refutation applies to C's no-go 'instruction cuts inside the walk loop: 0 at 4t on any CI model'. Reopen it as per-byte core-work changes (stores, loads, branches, replay), judged on 4-copy rows.
verdicts.corrected_recoverable: Walk-loop restructuring: lo 0, realized 3% (#181) to 5-14% (#171) of 4t wall, theoretical hi about 30%. Ir-only cuts of 3% or less: at most 1.5%, below the bench's resolution.

verdicts.claim: No-gos: more lanes / co-resident 16/L2 (0 or slower); longer prefetch distance (0); larger tile (worse); fused post-walk (0); psi^2 pair walk (premise: 'the per-core ceiling is now identified').
verdicts.reason:
Mixed.
- Survive on measurement: lanes / co-resident (sweeps flat at 4 copies; 16/L2 slower on 7 of 8 CPUs), tile (tile-size.md), fused post-walk (fused-postwalk.md).
- Prefetch distance survives for 4t only. Its premise 'latency already hidden' fails on Zen 5 at 1t (verdict 2).
- psi^2: the premise is refuted. The walk's 4t time tracks per-byte core work, so a pair walk's worth hinges on whether a 2-byte step costs less than two single steps in core work, not on lines. The prior CI losses (#6, #34) stand, and its rank (2) is not earned.
verdicts.corrected_recoverable: Lanes, hints, segments, tile, fused post-walk: 0 at 4t. psi^2: unknown sign, likely negative with its bigram build.

findings.front: D: the non-walk stages (Huffman/scanner, MTF+RLE2, T-vector build, RLE1, CRC, segment assembly) as dependency chains, priced as recoverable whole-decoder 4-thread wall on CI runners. Production decoder = d1fd4405 (#181). master 0769b52f, b7734313 and 4bfaf7cb have the same src/; `git diff d1fd4405 origin/master -- src examples Cargo.toml` is empty. Headline: at 4 threads CI's 4 vCPUs are saturated, so the 4t wall is the total co-run CPU divided by 4. On that basis the non-walk stages are 45-54% of the 4t wall on every runner measured. Ranked by recoverable 4t wall: (1) the MTF list chain, which a store-forwarding failure makes about 20-24 cycles a move. It is priced only, because a separate workflow owns MTF constructions: 2.4-9.4%. (2) The Huffman bit buffer, which this front found lives in memory. That puts a store-to-load forward on every table lookup: 0.6-4.1%, plus part of a 3-4% scanner-starvation idle. (3) The build's same-byte cursor chain and store drain: 0.4-5.0%. (4) The post-walk passes: 0-5%; #183's own runs put it near 1.4%. (5) Pipelining stages of different blocks on SMT siblings: unknown sign, about 0 on AMD and at most about 6.7% on Intel.

binding.claim: Regime: at 4 threads on CI all 4 vCPUs are saturated and no serial stage binds, so the 4t wall is the total co-run CPU divided by 4 (times 1/utilisation). A non-walk stage's 4t wall cost is its co-run CPU over 4, and its recoverable wall is its co-run CPU saved over 4, wherever the thread runs (the scanner included). Across all runners the non-walk stages (scanner, MTF, build, RLE1, CRC, assembly) come to 45-54% of the 4t wall.
binding.evidence: Utilisation, CPU/(4 x wall): 0.959 on 8573C (run 41980640481), 0.957 on 7763 (41986912287), 0.920 on 9V45 (41986885355), 0.970 on 8370C (41986908473). runq 0.37-0.40 s a run. 2t is saturated too (0.836 s CPU / 0.852 on 8573C). The scanner is not binding: busy 34-42% of the 4t wall, and in occupancy runs 41976148952 and 42009406264 the scanner waits on full slots and the reader is starved 77-79%. The stage shares are INFERRED: 4-copy factors from runs 42008210159 (8370C) and 42011789918 (7763), applied to each runner's 1t stage table, then split across the measured scanner and worker CPU. Non-walk share of 4t wall: 54.0% on 8573C, 45.0% on 7763, 45.7% on 9V45, 49.4% on 8370C. Cross-check: on 8573C the scanner's measured share of stage CPU at 4t is 11.25%, against 11.0% predicted.
binding.recoverable_4t_wall: framework, not itself recoverable. Ceiling if every non-walk stage cost nothing: 185 ms of 343 on 8573C. The floors (below) cap it at about 28% of the 4t wall.
binding.falsifier: A change that measurably cuts one stage's co-run CPU, such as the scanner's, where the 4t wall falls by less than half of (CPU saved)/4 across 2-3 runs.
binding.term_path: 4t wall <- total co-run CPU / 4 (saturated, runq > 0) <- sum over stages of (1t stage cost x co-run factor)

binding.claim: MTF (priced only; a separate workflow owns MTF constructions). Its time is a serial chain through the move-to-front list in memory. Each move's vector store and the following 1-byte store of the new front are read by the next move's two 32-byte loads, of base and base-1. A wide load over a narrower younger store cannot be forwarded, so it waits for the store to commit: about 20-24 cycles a move against a throughput bound of about 0.27 c/B. Floor with the list front held in a register: about 5 cycles a move, so MTF at about 0.8 c/B, about 40% of today.
binding.evidence: Code: src/mtf.rs:149-156 at d1fd4405 (blend store, then `*base = v`). The comment at src/mtf.rs:224-229 already says the next load 'can't be forwarded from it and waits for it to commit'. Local disassembly of mtf_avx2: `mov BYTE PTR [rsp+0x60],al`, then on the next move `vmovdqa ymm0,[rsp+0x60]` and `vpblendvb ...,[rsp+0x5f]`. Derivation: 15.15M moves; MTF 1t is 2.16 c/B on 8573C at its reported 3.0 GHz, which is 453M cycles. About 95M of that is run arithmetic, mispredicts on the run/move pattern, and memset/memmove calls for runs over 64 B and nn >= 32 (0.5M calls). That leaves about 23.6 cycles a move (about 21 on 7763, about 16 on 9V45). MTF is slowed by a busy sibling: co-run 1.54x on 8370C and 1.33x on 7763, so a latency chain does not get the sibling's idle slots for free. History fits the chain model: #170 cut 1.5% of decoder Ir and gained 4t wall -1.9% (-3.6,-0.2) on 7763 and 1t -2.1% (mtf-short-runs.md:57-66). #172 removed a load that fed only the counts and output, not the list chain, and was near noise (mtf-byte-list.md:115-129).
binding.recoverable_4t_wall: MTF's 4t share: 58 ms (17.0%) on 8573C, 60 ms (13.2%) on 7763, 28 ms (15.8%) on 9V45, 57 ms (14.4%) on 8370C. Recoverable: 1t MTF saving of 30-55% times 4t retention of 0.6-1.0 (a shorter chain gets less SMT benefit). 8573C 10.5-32 ms (3.1-9.4%); 7763 2.4-7.3%; 9V45 2.9-8.7%. Point about 5-6%. At 1t: 4.9-12.8%.
binding.falsifier: A construction with no store-to-wide-load on the list that cuts the 1t MTF stage by less than 15% refutes the commit-wait chain. An MTF stage cut of 30% or more that moves 4t wall by less than 1% refutes the regime rule for MTF.
binding.term_path: 4t wall <- worker CPU/4 <- MTF co-run cost (1.33-1.54x) <- 0.0722 moves/B x (store-forward-fail commit wait + blend) + run/move mispredicts

binding.claim: Huffman (scanner): the bit buffer is not in a register. In the 4-lookup unrolled loop each lookup stores buf and does a memory read-modify-write on live, and the next lookup reloads buf. So every lookup carries a store-to-load forward of about 4-5 cycles. The chain is then about 13-15 cycles a lookup (forward + shr + LUT load + and + `shl r64,cl`), against about 8-9 with buf in a register and a throughput bound of about 2-3. Probable cause: the cold non-inlined calls inside the loop take &mut Bits (Bits::refill_slow, Huff::decode_entry_slow), which stops LLVM promoting the struct to registers. The journals record no attempt at this.
binding.evidence: Local disassembly of read_item (rustc 1.97.0, d1fd4405): per step `shl rsi,cl; mov QWORD PTR [r15+0x18],rsi; sub DWORD PTR [r15+0x20],ecx`, then `mov rsi,QWORD PTR [r15+0x18]` at the next step, and the refill does `or rsi,QWORD PTR [r15+0x18]`. Code: src/bits.rs:49-50 (#[cold] refill_slow(&mut self)), src/block.rs:324-357 (step! macro, decode_entry_slow(e, br) at :343, br.refill() at :357). Counts: 0.0646 lookups/B, 83% pairs. Measured scanner 1t: 1.23 c/B (7763, run 42011789918), 1.49 (8370C, 42008210159), 418 ps/B (8573C), 234 ps/B (9V45). That is 19-23 cycles a lookup, of which about 15% is per-block headers, selectors and table builds. The scanner's 4t CPU is 0.12-0.14 s on 4 saturated vCPUs. Occupancy i:rd shows workers idle 3-4% of their time waiting for the scanner to finish a block (runs 41976148952 and 42009406264). The note at research-synthesis.md:104 that 'the whole scanner is 5.4%' is stale: it is 11-14% at 1t and 7-10% at 4t today.
binding.recoverable_4t_wall: Scanner's 4t share: 35 ms (10.3%) on 8573C, 31 ms (6.9%) on 7763, 16 ms (9.1%) on 9V45, 36 ms (9.2%) on 8370C. Recoverable: 1t scanner saving of 15-40% times 4t retention of 0.6-1.0. 8573C 3.2-14.1 ms (0.9-4.1%); 7763 0.6-2.8%; 9V45 0.8-3.6%. Point about 2.5%, plus up to about 1% from the i:rd starvation. At 1t: 1.7-5.6%. The cheapest and most certain mechanism on this front.
binding.falsifier: read_item with the bit state in locals (cold paths taking and returning it by value): a 1t stage-table scanner cut under 10% on CI refutes the store-forward chain (for example, memory renaming already hides it). A scanner cut of 25% or more where 4t CPU does not fall by about the scanner CPU saved refutes the regime. Precondition: check that CI's rustc 1.99.1 emits the same memory-resident buf.
binding.share_of_4t_wall: 7-10%, plus 3-4% worker idle tied to the scanner
binding.term_path: 4t wall <- scanner-thread CPU/4 (and i:rd idle) <- 0.0646 lookups/B x (store-forward on buf + LUT load + shift)

binding.claim: T-vector build: not a random scatter. It writes 256 sequential bucket streams, and 81.9% of rows go through the 16-row run path. At 1t its cost is a store-forward chain on ftab[c]: the 60.1% of one-row steps that repeat the previous byte reload a cursor stored one row earlier, about 5-6 cycles each, about 0.6 c/B. On top of that come the store throughput and line fills for 4n bytes of tt (3.6 MB a block, larger than every runner's L2). At 4t on Intel the build is the stage most hurt by a busy sibling (2.25x, worse than taking turns), which reads as store-drain/fill-buffer contention. On AMD 7763 it is SMT-friendly (1.43x). Floor: about 0.6-1.0 c/B of store throughput plus line fills, about 45-55% of today.
binding.evidence: Code: src/bwt.rs:304-312 (the one-row closure: ftab[c] loaded, s+1 stored) and :319 (the run16 test). Local disassembly: per row `mov edi,[rsp+r11+0x408]` ... `mov [rsp+r10*4+0x408],edi`. Census: same-byte rows 22.77M; run16 windows 10.74M. Co-run factors: 2.25x (8370C, run 42008210159) and 1.43x (7763, 42011789918). Build 1t share: 15-20% (8573C 582 ps/B, 7763 682). #169 cut the build stage 3.1% (Xeon 8573C) with no decoder gain (build-run-vectors.md:60-75). At the build's 4t share that predicts only 0.4-0.6% of wall, below resolution: a power null, not evidence that the build does not bind.
binding.recoverable_4t_wall: Build's 4t share: 69 ms (20.1%) on 8573C, 71 ms (15.6%) on 7763, 26 ms (14.3%) on 9V45, 75 ms (19.0%) on 8370C. Recoverable from breaking the same-byte chain (taking runs of 2-15 equal bytes with one cursor step, or interleaving 2-4 row ranges with cursors from mtf_checkpoints) plus run16 vector stores: 1t build saving of 10-25% times retention of 0.3-1.0 (low on Intel, where the co-run build is drain-bound). 8573C 2.1-17 ms (0.6-5.0%); 7763 0.5-3.9%; 9V45 0.4-3.6%. Point about 2%. At 1t: 1.5-5.0%.
binding.falsifier: A chain-breaking build that cuts the 1t build stage by 15% or more but moves 4t wall by under 0.5% on an Intel runner shows that the 4t build is drain-bound and the chain does not matter there. If the 1t build stage falls under 8%, the forward-chain reading is wrong.
binding.term_path: 4t wall <- worker CPU/4 <- build co-run cost (1.43-2.25x) <- 0.109 same-byte rows/B x ftab store-forward + 4 B/row of tt stores with line fills

binding.claim: Post-walk passes (segment assembly, RLE1, CRC) are not fused on master: three passes, 3n + 2m bytes. They have no meaningful chain. RLE1 here is a 32-wide compare plus a copy (12,029 runs in 209.7M bytes), and the CRC is 4 clmul fold lanes. All three are bandwidth- or line-fill-bound, and slowed by a busy sibling: RLE1 2.08x/1.53x, assembly 1.77x/2.97x, CRC 1.59x/1.41x (8370C/7763). The fusion was built and measured (#183). Its 4t effect is small but real on one Intel run.
binding.evidence: Code: src/lib.rs:349-353 (unrle, then crc32 re-reading out); fused-postwalk.md:9-16. #183 runs (fused-postwalk.md:138-143): PR run 1 (EPYC 7763) 4t -4.2% (-10.0,+1.8); PR run 2 (EPYC 9V45) +1.5% (-3.9,+7.2); fusion alone (Xeon 8370C) 4t -1.5% (-2.4,-0.6); 1t -1.1% to -2.5%, beyond noise in all of them.
binding.recoverable_4t_wall: Post-walk 4t share: 23 ms (6.6%) on 8573C, 42 ms (9.3%) on 7763 (assembly inflates 2.97x there), 11.5 ms (6.4%) on 9V45. Recoverable: 0 to about 55% of that share, i.e. 0-3.7% on 8573C and 0-5.1% on 7763. Measured pooled point about -1.4% (the three runs: -4.2, +1.5, -1.5).
binding.falsifier: Pooled over 3 or more fresh 4t runs of the fused head, a point estimate that is not faster.
binding.term_path: 4t wall <- worker CPU/4 <- (n read + n write) + (n read + m write) + m read, all bandwidth-bound and SMT-inflated

binding.claim: SMT co-residency differs by stage and by microarchitecture, and no compute chain gets a free ride beside a busy sibling. On Intel (8370C) the walk tolerates a sibling best (1.46x), while the build and RLE1 do worse than taking turns (2.25x, 2.08x). On AMD (7763) the walk is the stage most slowed (2.12x) and the build, MTF and scanner tolerate a sibling (1.33-1.43x). AMD Zen 4/5 walk-beside-walk is 2.03x/2.29x. So on AMD the walk is slowed about 2x whatever the sibling runs.
binding.evidence: Runs 42008210159 (8370C) and 42011789918 (7763), each stage's fastest of 5 passes, alone and as 4 pinned copies. Walk-beside-walk: runs 41989596336 (EPYC 9V74: 4.27 to 8.65 c/B) and 41989592674 (EPYC 9V45: 2.89 to 6.63 c/B), coresident-walk/ files. The plain single-chain walk inflates only 1.5-1.6x (8370C) and 1.17x (7763) in the same 4-copy runs.
binding.recoverable_4t_wall: No direct saving. It sets the retention factors used above and the price of pipelining (next entry).
binding.falsifier: A repeat 4-copy run on the same CPU models with factors moving by more than about 0.2 (for example the build under 1.8x on an 8370C) would show the factors are run-to-run noise or pairing-phase artefacts.
binding.term_path: stage co-run factor <- which per-core resource the stage uses (issue slots vs fill buffers/store drain) x what the sibling uses

binding.claim: Pipelining stages of different blocks on SMT siblings (the walk on one sibling, MTF/build/Huffman of another block on the other) is priced but unproven, and its sign is unknown. Today pairing is random; the walk is about 50% of worker co-run time, so the two halves would balance. On AMD there is no headroom for the walk, which is slowed about 2x beside any sibling. On Intel the upside is keeping the build away from walking siblings: at most the build's excess over about 1.5x, i.e. 69 ms x (1 - 1.5/2.25) = 23 ms. The cost is walks beside walks, unmeasured on today's kernel on Intel, which could cancel it. It is also a large structural change: stage-split workers pinned to siblings and topology detection.
binding.evidence: Factors from the entry above; worker mix from run 41980640481's thread split; walk-beside-walk on AMD only (runs 41989592674 and 41989596336).
binding.recoverable_4t_wall: AMD: about 0 (-2 to +2%). Intel: -3% to +6.7%. Not rankable until a pair matrix exists.
binding.falsifier: A pair-matrix measurement in which the build beside an MTF or Huffman sibling costs about as much as beside a walking sibling (within about 0.2x) on an Intel runner removes the whole upside.
binding.term_path: 4t wall <- sum over pairs of cost(X | sibling Y) <- pairing policy

findings.unknowns:
- No hardware counters on CI. The store-forward chains (MTF list, Huffman bit buffer, build cursor) and the build's store-drain reading are derived from disassembly plus counts plus measured cycles; they are not counted.
- The disassembly comes from local rustc 1.97.0. CI builds with 1.99.1, and the memory-resident Huffman buf is not yet confirmed on CI's codegen.
- Golden Cove-class cores (Xeon 8573C) may rename memory and hide the bit-buffer forward, so the Huffman gain could be smallest there.
- 4-copy co-run factors exist only for Xeon 8370C and EPYC 7763. Applying them to the 8573C (Intel family) and the 9V45 (AMD family) is a cross-model inference. There is no stage factor for the 9V74.
- The 4-copy harness pairs each stage with a sibling at an uncontrolled phase: copies drift, other-walk passes interleave, and taking each stage's fastest of 5 passes favours gentler pairings. The factors are therefore 'beside a mixed sibling', not the decoder's exact mix.
- The decoder's 4t CPU exceeds the 4-copy stage sum by about 10% (8370C) to about 50% (7763). Part of that is VM-to-VM variance: on the 7763 VMs the 1t walk differed by 14.6% between runs 41986912287 and 42011789918. Part is oversubscription, preemption and the harness's reader and hash. None of it is attributed to stages.
- The stage-pair matrix (X beside Y) is unmeasured, so the sign of pipelining is unknown.
- The MTF construction space belongs to the other workflow; the 30-55% MTF saving range here is a chain-model bound, not a tested construction.
- The census overcounts Huffman lookups by about 2.7% (each window's partial last block).
- i9: at 4 threads there is no SMT co-run, so its stage mix is like CI's 2t. Its many-copy figures are DRAM contention and were not used for CI.

verdicts.claim: Regime: the 4t wall is total co-run CPU / 4. A non-walk stage's recoverable 4t wall is its co-run CPU saved / 4. Non-walk stages are 45-54% of 4t wall on every runner.
verdicts.reason:
The aggregate part holds (OBSERVED). Utilisation is 0.919-0.970 (8573C 41980640481 0.959; 8370C 41986908473 0.970; 9V45 41986885355 attempt 2 0.919). Where both resolved, 4t wall moved with 4t CPU: #183 fusion alone on the 8370C, wall -1.5% against CPU -1.9%; #181 run 3 (41979947814) on the 9V45, -3.2% against -3.5%. The occupancy runs also back 'no serial stage binds': the scanner is in a slot wait for 40-47% of the span and the reader is starved for 77-79%.

The per-stage rule fails, for three reasons.

(a) A stage's co-run factor is not fixed when its own code changes. #171 changed only the walk. On the 9V45 it cut 4t CPU by 17.6% (run 41952512753 attempt 1) and 16.3% (41956321455 attempt 2), and amplification fell from 2.23x to 1.84x. At 1t the same runs moved -0.1% and +0.4%, and the walk stage +0.3% and +3.4%. So co-run cost can move with no change in alone time, and '1t saving x fixed factor' cannot be the recoverable model.

(b) The run totals do not pin down per-stage factors. On the 8573C, a factor set with build 1.50 and walk 1.72 reproduces the front's worker co-run sum (5302 ps/B) exactly, and moves the build's 4t share from 20.1% to 13.4%.

(c) The 7763 inputs come from a noisy VM. In 41986912287, 1t wall ranged 0.727-1.016 s and 4t 0.382-0.503 s across 10 rounds, and the run's own summary says 'a noisy run'. A clean 7763 on the same base the same morning (#183 run 1, 41986885355 attempt 1) gave 1t 0.692 s, 4t 0.314 s, amplification 1.69x. That noisy run is what produces the 'about 50%' excess of 4t CPU over the 4-copy sum in the front's unknowns. On clean runs, the 4-copy factors predict worker plus scanner CPU to within -7% to +4%: 8573C +4%, 9V45 +3.5%, 8370C -7% (walk split) or -2.6% (walk timed as one).

Recomputed non-walk share of 4t wall:
- 8573C: 53.6% (unscaled) to 56.4% (scaled to total CPU).
- 8370C: 41.6-51.5%. The walk's 4-copy factor is 1.45x timed in parts but 1.61x timed as one in the same run (42008210159).
- 9V45: 44.7-50.7% (7763 factors against 9V74 factors).
- 7763: about 45%, from the phases VM's alone table against the clean 0.314 s wall.
verdicts.corrected_recoverable: The 4t wall tracks total 4t CPU (OBSERVED). A stage's recoverable 4t wall is its own co-run saving plus an unmeasured change in what its sibling costs; for a footprint change (#171) the second term was the larger. The non-walk share is 42-56% of 4t wall depending on the factor set and method (INFERRED). On a clean 7763 the ms figures are about 30% smaller than the front's (0.314 s vs 0.453 s wall).

verdicts.claim: MTF (priced only): a store-forward chain of about 20-24 cycles a move. 4t recoverable 2.4-9.4%, with retention 0.6-1.0; 'a latency chain does not get the sibling's idle slots for free'.
verdicts.reason:
Nothing measures the 4t retention floor of 0.6. On AMD, MTF has the lowest co-run factor of any stage: 1.33x on the 7763 (42011789918) and 1.23x on the 9V74 (42020095581, a run the front did not have). So on AMD it largely shares the core with its sibling.

Across stages on AMD, latency-bound code has the low factors: the plain walk 1.18x on the 7763 and 1.28x on the 9V74, MTF 1.23-1.33x. Throughput- and memory-bound code has the high ones: the room walk 2.12-2.22x, assembly 2.97-3.53x. A chain cut makes the MTF that remains more throughput-bound, which should push its factor toward the decoder's average of 1.71-1.79x. Derivation (INFERRED): a 30% alone cut with the rest of MTF at 1.71x is 0.70 x 1.71 / 1.33 = 0.90 of today's MTF co-run time, a 10% saving. That is a retention of about 0.34, and it leaves out any added cost to the sibling.

The 95M cycles subtracted as overhead are asserted, not derived. The 4.29M runs alone could mispredict for about 130M cycles, so the chain could be 16-24 cycles a move rather than 23.6.

On Intel, MTF's factor (1.54x on the 8370C) is close to the average (1.62x), so retention near 1 is plausible there. The 8573C figures assume the 8370C factor carries across models, which is unchecked.
verdicts.corrected_recoverable: 8573C: 3.1-9.4%, if the 8370C factor applies. AMD (7763): about 1.3-7.3%, from 13.2% x 30% x 0.34 up to 13.2% x 55% x 1.0. Point estimate about 3-4%, not 5-6%.

verdicts.claim: Huffman bit buffer in memory: 0.6-4.1% of 4t wall, plus part of a 3-4% scanner-starvation idle (i:rd). 'The cheapest and most certain mechanism on this front.'
verdicts.reason:
The scanner's co-run cost is the best-pinned 4t term on the front, because it runs on its own thread (OBSERVED). Its 4t CPU against its 1t stage time:
- 9V45: 0.062 s against 0.049 s, 1.27x.
- 7763 (noisy run): 0.120 s against 0.081 s, 1.49x.
- 8573C: 0.135 s against 0.088 s, 1.54x.
- 8370C: 0.143 s against 0.087 s, 1.64x.

The starvation share is overstated. The occupancy JSONs split worker idle two ways: {no job, job queued} and {scanner reading, input, slot, outside}.
- 'i:rd' (4.15% on the 9V74, 3.45% on the 7763, timeline mode) includes time when a job was queued but the worker had not yet taken it (jobs_queued 2.43% and 1.68%).
- In parallel.rs:418-426 a worker holds the jobs Mutex while blocked in recv. So w.lock (3.49% and 3.00%) is mostly idle workers queued behind another idle worker.
- Workers idle with no job while the scanner reads come to 1.4-3.3% across the timeline and full modes.
- Of the scanner's 'reading' state (0.49-0.57 of the span), about 30% is the scanner itself off-CPU. For example, on the 7763, 0.170 s reading against about 0.12 s of CPU.

So a 15-40% scanner cut recovers about 0.1-0.9% of wall through i:rd, not about 1%.

'Most certain' is not shown. The bit-buffer store-forward comes from local rustc 1.97.0 disassembly, unconfirmed on CI's 1.99.1, with no counters. On the 9V45 the scanner's factor (1.27x) is below average, so the same retention argument as for MTF applies there.
verdicts.corrected_recoverable: 0.5-4.1% of 4t wall (low end on the 9V45: 9.1% x 15% x 0.35), plus at most about 0.9% from starvation.

verdicts.claim: T-vector build: the same-byte cursor chain at 1t. At 4t on Intel the build is 2.25x, 'worse than taking turns' and drain-bound (retention 0.3). Build share 14-20% of 4t wall; recoverable 0.4-5.0%.
verdicts.reason:
'Worse than taking turns' needs the sibling's slowdown during the build, which is unmeasured. The pair's throughput is 0.44 plus the sibling's speed. It is below 1 only if the sibling is also slowed 1.8x or more, which holds only if the 4-copy siblings ran build beside build, and the front itself calls that phase uncontrolled.

The 2.25x comes from one 8370C run, with copies at 2.07-2.33x, applied across models to the 8573C. Within AMD the build's factor moves by 0.33: 1.43x on the 7763 against 1.76x on the 9V74 (42020095581). That is beyond the front's own falsifier threshold of 0.2.

The 8573C share (20.1%) is not pinned down by the totals: 13.4% fits equally well (see the regime verdict). 'Drain-bound' is a reading of one factor, with no counter behind it.

The build scatters into 256 store streams (docs/ledger.md:20). That is the same pattern #171 removed from the walk, the change that gave the campaign's largest 4t gain. The front prices only the cursor chain and leaves that footprint unpriced.
verdicts.corrected_recoverable: Build 4t share: 13-20% on the 8573C (not pinned down), 14-17% on AMD. Recoverable from breaking the chain: 0.2-5%. A footprint (staging) change is unpriced and of unknown sign.

verdicts.claim: Post-walk passes (assembly, RLE1, CRC) unfused on master; #183 4t effect small but real on one Intel run; pooled about -1.4%.
verdicts.reason: OBSERVED, and the runs are cited correctly. On the 8370C the fusion alone transferred at 0.65 of its 1t gain in wall and 0.83 in CPU (1t -2.3%, 4t wall -1.5%, CPU -1.9%). That matches the stage's own share, with no extra relief for the sibling showing. Two corrections: the 7763's 42 ms (9.3%) comes from the noisy VM, and assembly's factor varies from 1.77x to 3.53x by model.
verdicts.corrected_recoverable: Unchanged: about 1.4% pooled, 0-5% bound.

verdicts.claim: SMT co-residency differs by stage and microarchitecture; no compute chain gets a free ride beside a busy sibling; on Intel the walk tolerates a sibling best (1.46x); on AMD the walk is slowed about 2x whatever the sibling runs (walk-beside-walk 2.03x/2.29x).
verdicts.reason:
The factor values themselves are right; I reproduced them from the artifacts. The conclusions drawn from them fail.

(a) The runs labelled 'walk-beside-walk' (41989596336 on the 9V74, 41989592674 on the 9V45) come from examples/sweep.rs (0769b52f, lines 150-160). There every copy runs MTF, the build, the timed walk and RLE1 for each block, so the walk's sibling is a mix of stages at an uncontrolled phase, just as in phases. No run separates walk beside walk from walk beside another stage. 'Whatever the sibling runs' is therefore unsupported.

(b) 'No compute chain gets a free ride': MTF is 1.23x on the 9V74, and the plain single-chain walk is 1.18x on the 7763 and 1.28x on the 9V74.

(c) 'On Intel the walk tolerates a sibling best': the walk timed as one is 1.61x in the same 8370C run (42008210159; copies 1.57-1.65x), against 1.46x timed in parts. That gap comes from taking the fastest of 5 passes for each stage separately. At 1.61x the walk is not distinguishable from the scanner (1.56x), MTF (1.54x) or the CRC (1.59x). On AMD the two timings agree (2.12/2.13x, 2.22/2.21x).

(d) The factors differ by more than 0.2 within AMD across models, so Zen 3's factors cannot stand in for the 9V45 (Zen 5).
verdicts.corrected_recoverable: Not applicable. The per-run factors are observed, each 'beside a mixed sibling at uncontrolled phase'. Which sibling causes a slowdown is unmeasured on every model.

verdicts.claim: Pipelining stages on SMT siblings: AMD about 0 (-2 to +2%), because the walk is slowed about 2x beside any sibling; Intel -3% to +6.7%; the walk is about 50% of worker co-run time, so the halves balance.
verdicts.reason:
The AMD bound rests on claim 6's sibling-independence, which nothing measures.

The walk is 55-60% of worker co-run time, not about 50%: 54.6% on the 8370C, 58.5% on the 7763, 59.7% on the 9V74 (from the phases 4-copy tables). So the two halves do not balance.

INFERRED model, 7763 phases VM, 2 files a core: walk alone 4.33 c/B, non-walk 5.91 c/B including the scanner, non-walk beside non-walk 1.38x. An ideal pairing of walk against non-walk gives:
- walk beside non-walk 1.2x, non-walk beside walk 1.4x: core time 13.4 against 17.46 today, -23%;
- 2.0x and 1.4x: 16.9, -3%;
- 2.2x and 1.6x: 19.0, +9%.

The Intel +6.7% uses the cross-model build share. It also assumes the build's excess comes from walking siblings, which is unmeasured. Only the front's conclusion, 'not rankable until a pair matrix exists', survives.
verdicts.corrected_recoverable: Sign and size unknown on both vendors. On AMD the bound is about -23% to +9% (INFERRED), not about 0.

falsifier.missed:
1. A third phases run exists that the front did not have: 42020095581 (EPYC 9V74, 4bfaf7cb, another front's dispatch). Its factors:
   - scanner 1.32x, MTF 1.23x, build 1.76x;
   - walk 2.22x (2.16x without assembly);
   - RLE1 1.86x, CRC 1.37x, assembly 3.53x;
   - total 1.79x.
   AMD factors therefore differ by model by more than 0.2.

2. The largest 4t lever so far was a change in co-run cost, not in alone time. #171 on the 9V45: 4t CPU -17.6% and -16.3%, wall -14.4% and -13.9%, with 1t flat. The 7763 runs gained 10-13% at 4t, alongside 7-13% at 1t; the 8573C 5.2% at 4t and 4.7% at 1t. That is pre-#180, but CPU measures co-run cost directly.
   - The front's whole ranking assumes fixed factors.
   - It never prices cuts to the high factors in non-walk stages: the build's 256-stream scatter (2.25x on the 8370C, 1.76x on the 9V74; the store pattern #171 removed from the walk), RLE1 (1.53-2.08x) and assembly (1.77-3.53x).
   - The journals record no staged-build experiment.

3. The job handoff is serialised. In src/parallel.rs:418-426 (d1fd4405) a worker holds the jobs Mutex<Receiver> while blocked in recv.
   - At 4t: w.lock 3.0-3.5% and 'idle with a job queued' 1.7-2.4% of worker time (occupancy 42009406264 and 41976148952, timeline mode).
   - At 2t: w.lock 0.8-0.9% and job-queued idle 0.06%.
   - split-condvars measured the condvar, not this Mutex, and on a non-SMT local VM.
   - Ceiling for all worker idle (4.1-5.7% of worker time) is about 2-3% of 4t wall (INFERRED). The ratio comes from #180: 18 points more worker-busy bought 8-10% of wall.

4. Each block at 4t is preempted about once: 0.82-0.99 timeslices and 0.27-0.35 ms in the run queue, 12.5-13.4% of decode elapsed (full mode). So 'decoding 92-93%' means about 80-81% of the span actually on CPU decoding. The refill cost after each preemption is spread over the stages without being named.

5. SMT gives only 1.13-1.24x from 2t to 4t: 8573C 1.244, 8370C 1.162, 9V45 1.126, noisy 7763 1.128.
   - The 4t wall is the two-core wall divided by that small gain.
   - A stage's 4t share differs from its 1t share only through its own SMT gain, which the totals cannot identify.

6. A mix-shift term the additive model omits. Shrinking non-walk work makes a walk's sibling more often another walk. If a walk beside a walk is slowed more than a walk beside another stage, that offsets part of every non-walk saving: plausibly 0-30% on AMD, unmeasured (INFERRED).

7. Inputs and method.
   - The 7763 figures come from the noisy run 41986912287; use #183 run 1 (41986885355 attempt 1) instead.
   - Taking each stage's fastest of 5 passes separately biases the per-part 4-copy factors low on Intel, by about 0.15 for the walk.
   - The front's i9 description checks out: plan_with(4, 10 cores) is Workers(4).

findings.front: E: no-go archaeology. I listed every rejected or parked decoder idea in the journals, PRs and research branches. For each one I name what the no-go was of, which premises have changed since, the predicted direction now and the cheapest decisive test. Candidates are ranked by P(flip) x recoverable 4-thread wall on the CI runners. Result: two candidates are live and worth CI time. P74-C (an MTF list head held in a ymm register) was archived on registration gates and never put through the CI PR bench. The fused post-walk (#183) failed on its decision rule and power, not on its mechanism. A third, the write-only (first-column) build scatter, is weaker; its premise changed when #114 shipped. Two new no-gos come from measurement: cooperative teams on CI lose about 29% (observed), and every scheduling idea is capped at about 4% because the 4-thread decode is CPU-saturated.
